records.question: Why did capital expenditure rise in 2025?
records.expected_answer: Larger projects: the Pennine theatre complex, the emergency department rebuild at St Wystan's and the MRI replacement at Alderbank

answer.answer: Capital expenditure rose to 96.4 million pounds in 2025 (up from 71.0 million in 2024) because the group undertook major building and equipment projects: the new theatre complex at Pennine Orthopaedic Centre (opened on schedule in the autumn), the rebuilding of the emergency department at St Wystan's Hospital, and the replacement of the MRI scanners at Alderbank General Hospital. The Chair's review also notes agency staffing savings were redirected into opening additional beds and extending evening clinics.

citations.quote: Capital expenditure reached 96.4 million pounds, up from 71.0 million pounds in 2024.
The largest projects were the new theatre complex at Pennine Orthopaedic Centre
rebuilding of the emergency department at St Wystan's Hospital and the replacement of the MRI scanners
The money saved was used to open additional beds and to extend evening clinics.

answer.judge_reason: Identifies the same three major projects (Pennine theatre complex, St Wystan's emergency department rebuild, Alderbank MRI replacement) as the cause.
